- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecasts are flat or rising slowly, reduce forecast slope to avoid overestimating price rise.
- After a sharp spike in price (true outcome > 75), model tends to overcorrect — reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 3–5 days to avoid overshoot.
- If official event net supply is negative and bullish sentiment is high, model often underestimates price — increase forecast by 1–3% to align with sentiment-driven momentum.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and model forecasts are rising, reverse direction or reduce slope — bearish sentiment suppresses upward momentum.
- Model often fails to capture early spikes — if true outcome spikes > 5% above 30d mean, adjust forecast to include 1–2 day lagged spike in next 5–7 days.
- When supply net is negative and bullish sentiment is low, model tends to underreact — increase forecast by 1–2% to reflect muted sentiment.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often averages out — adjust forecast to reflect recent sentiment dominance (e.g., if last 3 days bullish, forecast should trend up).
